items.title: Wayne Bergeron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 29, 2020
items.q: I just pulled out my Maynard Ferguson tour jacket from 1986... I played on his final CD as a guest you know. He got me in and he did a tune on one of my CDs with me, six months before he passed away.

ctx.x: Did the fact that you started on the French horn have anything to do with that you could seem to play naturally high when you got to the trumpet?

It most definitely did. Because of the shape of that French horn mouthpiece and the depth of it. And when I went to a mouthpiece that had a cup way up here, and I just tried to play it the same way, I mean I was just learning how to play, but I started squeaking these funny sounds. You know I was squeaking these high notes and I couldn’t make a note in the lower register. So it got to where that became something I could do. And that’s probably why I still play, because I got a lot of attention for doing this. You…

Oh that’s very cute. I can just picture being, you know, like a lot of people I’ve done my share of adjudications at high school festivals. I can just picture that. Like gee that was a high note but are you sure you want him playing that?
